Other Perennial veggies...? Depends on your climate. If you live in a warm enough zone, tomatoes and peppers are perennials - but in most parts of the US they will die off in winter unless you have them covered.

Kale can be a perennial - I have kale that survived overwintered a couple of years. Chards too. Asparagus, Nettles, Artichokes, Cattails, Sweet potatoes (if you leave some in the ground they come up again), etc. Many herbs are winter-hardy and perennial. Perennial vegetables are a little uncommon, because most of the stuff we consider veggies have been cultivated annually.

Fruit trees and berries are perennial.

As an alternative, you might consider growing self-seeding annuals - like walking onions, miners lettuce, mache, sorrel, arugula, etc.
